author: ValWood
body:
Claude review:

PMID:20031578 is a genome-wide association study (GWAS) by Paré et al. (2009). It looked for genetic variants linked to plasma homocysteine levels; it did not test what the proteins do. It confirmed known associations with MTHFR and CBS, and found new ones at CPS1, MUT, NOX4 and DPEP1. 
(https://ora.ox.ac.uk/objects/uuid:028683e7-bf7f-45ef-b94c-92b1f231bc51)

Well established from other sources: CBS and MTHFR.

CBS (cystathionine β-synthase) is a core enzyme of homocysteine metabolism. It joins homocysteine with serine to make cystathionine, the first step in turning homocysteine into cysteine. Inherited CBS deficiency causes classical homocystinuria.
MTHFR makes 5-methyltetrahydrofolate. Methionine synthase uses this to turn homocysteine back into methionine. The common C677T variant raises homocysteine, and severe MTHFR deficiency causes homocystinuria.
Both have direct enzyme assays, disease genetics and mouse models behind them. Even before this paper, variants in MTHFR and CBS were known to affect homocysteine levels. 
[cvtisr](https://ersearch2.cvtisr.sk/vufind/SummonRecord/FETCH-LOGICAL-c4827-132b58705bc90bf48059cc8b9c7a2d01ab7711da59d7cacfdfe08ed1b31733e73/Details?lng=en)

Repeatedly linked by genetics, but with no known biochemical role: CPS1, MMUT, NOX4 and DPEP1.

Replication: a later meta-analysis of 44,147 people confirmed the loci at or near MTHFR, MTR, CPS1, MUT, NOX4, DPEP1 and CBS. A GWAS in African Americans replicated NOX4, and replicated CPS1 in women only, which supports a sex-specific effect at that locus. 
[nih](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4321227)
[nature](https://www.nature.com/articles/s10038-017-0384-9/email/correspondent/c1/new)
MMUT uses a vitamin B12 cofactor but sits in propionate metabolism, not the homocysteine pathway. Isolated MMUT deficiency usually causes methylmalonic acidemia without high homocysteine. Any link is probably indirect, for example through B12 status.
CPS1 is the first enzyme of the urea cycle. The associated variant also affects glycine and other metabolites, so its effect on homocysteine is probably indirect.
DPEP1 is a kidney dipeptidase that breaks down glutathione-related dipeptides. It may affect how the kidney handles sulfur amino acids, but this hasn't been shown.
NOX4 is an NADPH oxidase that makes reactive oxygen species. No direct role in homocysteine metabolism is known. Most published work goes the other way: high homocysteine raises NOX4 activity.


I don't think a GWAS can be used with IDA evidence,  can it @pgaudet 
or even at all?
title: Annotations from PMID:20031578
